long_biography.plain_text:
Buying struggling businesses became Michel Cadrin's signature as he expanded Groupe Michel Cadrin across Quebec. Trained as a pharmacist, he moved from employee to partner and pharmacy owner before purchasing the financially troubled Brunet chain. The experience shaped an acquisition style based on finding usable assets and rebuilding underperforming operations.

Cadrin carried his regional involvement beyond company ownership. He served on Quebec City airport's board and joined local partners in co-owning the Quebec Remparts hockey club. The group held that interest through a wholly owned financial company. Quebec's business community later inducted him into the Académie des Grands Québécois, recognising a career whose holdings and employment remained concentrated in the province.
